fuel_phase.quote: The experiment is conducted with gas-fueled flames, both with and without a coflow of air.

measurements.quote: Measurements, as a function of the field strength and fuel, are taken of the ion current through the flame and the flame’s response time to electric forcing.
Measurements, as a function of the field strength and fuel, are taken of the ion current through the flame and the flame’s response time to electric forcing.
Voltage-current curves were recorded to assess the relationship between electric field strength and chemi-ion current, revealing ion-driven convection effects.
High-resolution cameras captured flame shape, luminosity, and soot distribution.
Spectral imaging with filters measures chemiluminescent emissions and soot volume fraction.
There were thermopile detectors to measure flame radiant emissions.

objective_summary.value: The investigation aims to better understand the relationship between electric field voltage and chemi-ion current, analyze flame dynamic responses to electric field changes, evaluate soot formation, and characterize stabilized near-limit lifted flames.
objective_summary.quote: The objective of this investigation is to better understand the relationship between electric field voltage and chemi-ion current, analyze the dynamic response of flames to electric field changes, evaluate soot formation, and characterize stabilized near-limit lifted flames.

key_findings.value: Recording voltage-current curves assessed the relationship between electric field strength and chemi-ion current, revealing ion-driven convection effects.
key_findings.quote: Voltage-current curves were recorded to assess the relationship between electric field strength and chemi-ion current, revealing ion-driven convection effects.

earth_applications.value: Using electric fields to control flames can reduce harmful pollutant production and fuel consumption, enabling more efficient terrestrial combustion.
earth_applications.quote: The use of electric fields to control flames can reduce the production of harmful pollutants in practical terrestrial combustion.
